storage_cors_b2_description: Run `b2 bucket update <bucket> --cors-rules "$(cat cors.json)"`, or paste the rules into the bucket's CORS settings in the web console. B2 uses its own field names and its own operation values rather than the S3 ones.
storage_cors_caveat: PUT covers uploads, GET and HEAD cover downloads. The Range request header and the exposed Content-Range and Accept-Ranges are what let PDF previews load a page at a time instead of the whole file.
storage_cors_minio_description: Save the rule as cors.xml and run `mc cors set <alias>/<bucket> cors.xml`. Per-bucket CORS needs AIStor; on community MinIO set MINIO_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN on the server instead, as a comma-separated list of origins.
storage_cors_notice: Uploads and previews go straight from the browser to the bucket, so the bucket has to allow this app's origin. A bucket with no CORS rule rejects every upload at the preflight, and the app can only report it as a generic network error. Pick your provider, paste the rule into the bucket, then retry the upload.
storage_cors_other_description: DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, Scaleway and other S3-compatible providers implement the same CORS API. Use the Amazon S3 rules as cors.json, wrapped in a CORSRules object, and point the CLI at your endpoint.
storage_cors_r2_description: Cloudflare dashboard → R2 → your bucket → Settings → CORS policy → Edit. Or run `wrangler r2 bucket cors put <bucket> --file cors.json`.
storage_cors_s3_description: S3 console → your bucket → Permissions → Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) → Edit. The console takes the bare array; the AWS CLI wants it wrapped in a CORSRules object, as `aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket <bucket> --cors-configuration file://cors.json`.
